notes: ROBOTS: www2.hm.com/robots.txt names ClaudeBot / Claude-Web / anthropic-ai, but that UA group ends in 'Allow: /' - H&M explicitly PERMITS Claude. No Claude-specific disallow, so no section-5 stop condition. ACCESS: all HTML page routes are hard-blocked (Akamai Bot Manager behavioural sensor, then outright 403) - curl_cffi safari18_0_ios/chrome, r.jina.ai (403 Access Denied), www2-hm-com.translate.goog (403), WebFetch (403). Two routes ARE open and carried the whole job: (a) the en_gb sitemap set (https://www2.hm.com/en_gb.sitemap.xml -> en_gb.pages.subdepartment.0-31.xml, 3010 URLs, 333 under /en_gb/home) gave the authoritative category tree; (b) the storefront's own Elevate PLP JSON endpoint https://api.hm.com/search-services/v1/en_GB/listing/resultpage?pageSource=PLP&page=1&sort=RELEVANCE&pageId=<path>&page-size=36&touchPoint=DESKTOP&categoryId=x , which is NOT behind Akamai, returns GBP prices and the en_gb assortment, and exposes plpList.numberOfHits - the same field the PLP header renders. SLUG TRAP: the en_gb *URL* branch is /shop-by-product/furniture/... (singular) but the API pageId namespace uses the /shop-by-product/furnitures/... form (the en_us/en_ie slug); 'furniture' returns 0 hits, 'furnitures' returns the real data. Likewise URL leaf tables/side-table.html maps to API pageId tables/side. Every 'link' below is the canonical en_gb origin URL, confirmed live and confirmed to be the right node by its indexed page title (e.g. 'Side Tables | Nesting, Marble, Lamp & End Tables | H&M GB'), never the API path. QTY SOURCE: section-4 method 2 (structured), because the rendered header is unreachable. Sanity checks run: (1) discrimination - bogus pageIds (/home/shop-by-product/thisdoesnotexist12345, .../furnitures/nonsense999) return numberOfHits=0 while real ones vary widely (home=3961, decorations=1042, lighting=167, furnitures=301, ladies/dresses=1354), so the number tracks the category and is not a site-wide constant; (2) the categoryId param is ignored - pageId alone drives the result (5 different categoryIds returned byte-identical responses), so no stale-category risk from it; (3) two reads several minutes apart gave identical values for all 16 counted leaves - no drift; (4) children sum sanely to parents: storage 22+36+3=61 = storage total exactly; tables 6+34+4+32+61=137 vs 138; chairs 14+1+16+15+4+1+9+4=64 vs 74; the three branches 74+138+61=273 vs the Furniture total of 301, i.e. ~28 products (pedestals, footstools, display shelves, media units, a headboard) sit directly on the parent with no child node - no child count is ever above its parent; (5) corroboration with the prior Home-Decor pass: Mirrors was verified at 39 there via __NEXT_DATA__ productListingData.totalHits; this API returns 38 today - same field, ordinary drift. TREE: shop-by-product/furniture is the only furniture department; its three children (Chairs & Seating, Storage, Tables) all have real children, so per section 2 they are grouping rows and only the 17 leaves carry qty+URL. furniture/view-all.html dropped per section 3. ROOM DUPLICATES EXCLUDED (verified by product-ID overlap, not assumed): shop-by-room/livingroom/furniture (203 hits, 170 of its 187 products already inside the shop-by-product furniture catalogue), shop-by-room/outdoor/furniture (19 hits, 18 of 19 already inside it - H&M has no separate outdoor-furniture assortment, just metal/concrete side tables and a deck chair also filed under Tables/Chairs), and shop-by-room/kids-room/furniture-lighting (29 hits, 25 already inside it, and it is an unsplit furniture+lighting roll-up containing 3 lamps). All three would double-count. ALSO EXCLUDED per section 1: shop-by-product/storage/* (baskets, boxes, jars, kitchen storage, laundry baskets, wall-storage = standalone storage goods, not storage furniture), the shop-by-room/*/storage room views (same goods), all lighting, decorations (mirrors, frames, posters, vases, plant pots, trays), textiles, bed-linen, bath-shower, cooking-dining, flowers-plants, home-fragrance, homewear/sleepwear, giftwraps, and every seasonal-trending / holiday / christmas / sale / bestsellers / brands / premium landing page (section 3). H&M Home sells no beds, mattresses or bathroom vanity units.
